[[Club Bolívar|Bolívar]] were the defending champions, having won the [[2016–17 Liga de Fútbol Profesional Boliviano season#Torneo Clausura 2017|2017 Clausura]] tournament. In the Torneo Apertura, [[C.D. Jorge Wilstermann|Jorge Wilstermann]] won their fourteenth league title, and seventh in the professional era, after beating [[The Strongest]] on penalties in the third and last match of the finals on 6 June,{{cite web|url=https://www.lostiempos.com/deportes/futbol/20180607/wilstermann-nuevo-monarca-del-futbol|language=Spanish|publisher=[[Los Tiempos]]|date=6 June 2018|title=Wilstermann, el nuevo monarca del fútbol}} and [[Club San José|San José]] won their fourth league title in the Torneo Clausura on 19 December after tying with [[Royal Pari FC|Royal Pari]] by a 1–1 score.{{cite web|url=https://www.diez.bo/futbol/San-Jose-es-el-nuevo-campeon-del-futbol-boliviano-20181219-0023.html|language=Spanish|publisher=diez.bo|date=19 December 2018|title=San José es el nuevo campeón del fútbol boliviano}} ==Format== Given that the league was expanded from 12 to 14 teams, the league format had a slight variation for this season. The ''Torneo Apertura'' was played in the first half of the year, with the 14 teams being split into two groups of seven teams each for the first stage, in which teams in each group played each other as well as a team from the other group (their derby rival) twice, for a total of 14 matches. The top four teams from each group qualified for the knockout stage, where they were sorted in four ties played on a home-and-away basis, with the four winners advancing to the semifinals and the winners of each semifinal advancing to the final of the tournament. The six teams that failed to qualify for the knockout stage played another separate knockout tournament for a berth to the [[Copa Sudamericana]].{{cite news|url=https://www.lostiempos.com/deportes/futbol/20180106/liga-define-torneo-interseries-preve-entregar-cuatro-premios|title=La Liga define torneo interseries y prevé entregar cuatro premios|date=5 January 2018|publisher=Los Tiempos|language=Spanish}} On the other hand, the ''Torneo Clausura'' was played in the second half of the year under a double round-robin system, with all teams playing each other twice for a total of 26 matches.{{cite news|url=https://www.diez.bo/futbol/El-torneo-Clausura-se-jugara-todos-contra-todos-20180105-0022.html|title=El torneo Clausura se jugará todos contra todos|date=5 January 2018|publisher=diez.bo|language=Spanish}} International qualification was as follows: the champions and runners-up of each tournament qualified for the [[2019 Copa Libertadores]], while the third-placed team in each tournament, as well as the fourth-placed in the Clausura and the winners of the Apertura's secondary knockout tournament would qualify for the [[2019 Copa Sudamericana]]. ==Teams== The number of teams for the 2018 season was increased by two, from twelve to fourteen. [[Club Aurora|Aurora]] and [[Royal Pari FC|Royal Pari]] were promoted to the top flight after winning the [[2016–17 Copa Simón Bolívar]] and [[2017 Copa Simón Bolívar]], respectively. [[Club Petrolero|Petrolero]] was relegated to the [[Bolivian Football Regional Leagues#Tarija Football Association Championship|ATF Championship]] after losing the [[2016–17 Liga de Fútbol Profesional Boliviano season#Relegation/promotion playoff|relegation playoff]] to [[Club Destroyers|Destroyers]], the 2016–17 Copa Simón Bolívar runner-up. {{location map+ |Bolivia |float=right |width=300 |caption=Locations of the 2018 Primera División teams. |places= {{location map~ |Bolivia |lat=-17.379201 |long=-66.161679 |label=
